name: Apple and Tapioca Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: apples, juicy and well-flavored pippins, pared and cored
ingredients.originalText: 6 apples, juicy and well-flavored pippins, pared and cored

instructions.text: Cover the tapioca with three cups of lukewarm water, and set it in a tolerably warm place to soak five or six hours, stirring now and then.
Pack your apples in a deep dish, adding a cup of lukewarm water; cover closely and steam in a moderate oven until soft all through, turning them as they cook at bottom.
If the dish is more than a quarter full of liquid, turn some of it out before you pour the soaked tapioca over all.
Unless your apples are very sweet fill the centre with sugar and stick a clove in each, just before you cover with the tapioca.
Bake, after the tapioca goes in, one hour.
Eat warm, with sweet hard sauce.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cover the tapioca with three cups of lukewarm water, and set it in a tolerably warm place to soak five or six hours, stirring now and then.
2. Pack your apples in a deep dish, adding a cup of lukewarm water; cover closely and steam in a moderate oven until soft all through, turning them as they cook at bottom.
3. If the dish is more than a quarter full of liquid, turn some of it out before you pour the soaked tapioca over all.
4. Unless your apples are very sweet fill the centre with sugar and stick a clove in each, just before you cover with the tapioca.
5. Bake, after the tapioca goes in, one hour.
6. Eat warm, with sweet hard sauce.
